findings.description: From ~2.0s to ~4.25s the real man is drawing a dark comb-like object through the hair above his temple, while his reflection holds a small white blade pressed flat across the forehead, lower than the real hand and as a different-coloured object. A mirror cannot show a different object or a different contact point.

At ~9.0s the real hand hangs below the chin, seemingly empty and not touching the face, while the reflection presses the razor against the jaw. At several other points (e.g. 0.0s, 1.0s, 7.0s) the real hand is at the chin or jaw while the reflection's razor is at the upper lip or nose. The reflection's hand pose does not track the real hand.

In the reflection the man appears to scrape a blade across his forehead and brow from ~2.0s to ~4.25s, which isn't a plausible shaving motion. Throughout the clip he 'shaves' dry, with no lather and no change to his stubble, so the action reads as nonsensical.
